name: Durasphere pivotal trial
question: Does transurethral Durasphere provide comparable stress-incontinence improvement to bovine collagen in women with intrinsic sphincter deficiency?

design.blinding: Patients and outcome evaluators blinded; injectors unblinded
design.population: Women with stress urinary incontinence due to intrinsic sphincter deficiency and abdominal leak-point pressure below 90 cm H2O.
design.description: Multicenter, patient- and evaluator-blinded randomized equivalence trial
design.locator: PubMed abstract, Methods; FDA SSED pp7,9

verdictNote: Authors reported equivalence; the FDA tables present difference tests without equivalence intervals.
takeaway: Durasphere carbon-coated zirconium-oxide beads and bovine collagen yielded similar 12-month continence-grade and pad-weight improvement in women with intrinsic sphincter deficiency. Durasphere required less injected material but caused more early urgency and retention.

reports.label: Initial randomized report
reports.dateLocator: PubMed citation: July 2001; day approximated as first of month
reports.citation: Lightner D, Calvosa C, Andersen R, et al. "A new injectable bulking agent for treatment of stress urinary incontinence: results of a multicenter, randomized, controlled, double-blind study of Durasphere." *Urology.* 2001;58(1):12-15. doi:10.1016/s0090-4295(01)01148-7
reports.followUp: 12 months after initial injection for the primary endpoints; one year after last treatment for a smaller reported subset
reports.followUpLocator: PubMed abstract, Results; FDA SSED pp7,12-13

results.measure: At least one-grade improvement at 12 months after initial injection
results.note: Author-reported equivalence; FDA review describes a 15-percentage-point margin but gives a test for difference, not an equivalence interval.
results.locator: FDA SSED pp7,12, Table 3; PubMed abstract, Results

results.measure: Mean reduction in standardized pad weight from baseline to 12 months after initial injection
results.note: Author-reported equivalence; the FDA table reports a difference test without an equivalence interval.
results.locator: FDA SSED p13, Table 4; PubMed abstract, Results

results.measure: At least one-grade improvement one year after last treatment
results.note: Treatment-anchored subset; distinct from the initial-injection primary endpoint.

harms.label: Urinary urgency lasting more than 24 hours, any attribution
harms.locator: FDA SSED p15, Table 6 and text below table
harms.note: Short-term risk was higher with Durasphere (P=0.002).

harms.label: Acute retention lasting more than 24 hours and at most seven days, any attribution
harms.locator: FDA SSED p15, Table 6 and text below table
harms.note: Short-term risk was higher with Durasphere (P<0.001).

delivery.label: Initial injected volume
delivery.locator: PubMed abstract, Results; FDA SSED p14
delivery.note: P<0.001 for the between-agent volume difference.

delivery.label: Injection technique
delivery.value: Durasphere was injected transurethrally under endoscopic vision into the bladder-neck submucosa; up to four retreatments were allowed.
